summary: On paper Kansas City has the edge (Kansas City's defense ranks 16th in EPA per dropback with motion, +0.08 allowed). The model favors Kansas City at 61%, mostly on rushing matchup (2.1 pts) and passing matchup (1.1 pts).

KC.detail: Kansas City's defense ranks 16th in EPA per dropback with motion (+0.08 allowed). Miami ranks 26th (+0.07).

MIA.detail: Miami ranks 26th in EPA per dropback with motion (+0.07). Kansas City's defense ranks 16th (+0.08 allowed).

team_cards.t1: Miami has the 2nd-worst motion passing game.
team_cards.t2: Kansas City can lean on that.
team_cards.source: NFLVERSE PLAY-BY-PLAY · FTN CHARTING VIA NFLVERSE
team_cards.note: Garbage time removed · KC: n=35 dropbacks

model.summary: Model: Kansas City 61% to win, fair line KC -3.5. Market: Kansas City 82%. The largest factor is rushing matchup, worth 2.1 points toward Kansas City.

model_cards.t1: The model likes Miami more than the market.
model_cards.sub: Win probability. Market = vig-free moneyline at build time.
model_cards.source: NFLVERSE PLAY-BY-PLAY · INJURIES · SNAP COUNTS · SCHEDULES (LINES)
model_cards.note: Not betting advice · market line at build time

model_cards.sub: Each factor's push on the projected margin, in points. Positive = toward Miami. Sum = KC -3.5.
model_cards.source: NFLVERSE PLAY-BY-PLAY · INJURIES · SNAP COUNTS · SCHEDULES (LINES)
model_cards.note: Linear model, so contributions are exact SHAP values · vs. an average matchup

model_cards.sub: Distribution of Miami's margin. Shaded area = Miami win (39%).
model_cards.source: NFLVERSE PLAY-BY-PLAY · INJURIES · SNAP COUNTS · SCHEDULES (LINES)
model_cards.note: Normal margin, sigma = 12.0 points (fit by log loss)

model_cards.t1: Miami is missing 1.4 starters' worth of snaps.
model_cards.t2: Injuries move the line 1.0 points toward Kansas City.
model_cards.sub: Players listed Out, Doubtful or Questionable, weighted by recent snap share. QBs are in the QB factor.
model_cards.source: NFLVERSE PLAY-BY-PLAY · INJURIES · SNAP COUNTS · SCHEDULES (LINES)
model_cards.note: Weight = snap share (last 4 games) x status (Out 1.0, Doubtful 0.85, Questionable 0.25)

model_cards.t1: The biggest unit gap: Kansas City's pass defense.
model_cards.t2: 0.04 EPA per play better than Miami's.
model_cards.sub: Opponent-adjusted EPA per play vs. league average, the inputs to the model. Right = better.
model_cards.source: NFLVERSE PLAY-BY-PLAY · INJURIES · SNAP COUNTS · SCHEDULES (LINES)
model_cards.note: Recency-weighted, last season's plays at 35% weight

model_cards.t2: It trails the market: Brier 0.226 vs. 0.211.
model_cards.sub: Walk-forward backtest, 2018-2025 (2087 games). Each season uses only earlier data.
model_cards.source: NFLVERSE PLAY-BY-PLAY · INJURIES · SNAP COUNTS · SCHEDULES (LINES)
model_cards.note: Brier score: lower is better · market = closing line
